title: Diminishing returns to fertiliser
question: Per country (latest year, arable land ≥ 200,000 ha, ≤ 800 kg/ha): is cereal yield (kg/ha) an increasing, saturating function of fertiliser use (kg/ha of arable land), and does the grain per kg of fertiliser fall as use rises?

issues.text: Countries that use more fertiliser are also richer, more irrigated and use better seed: the curve mixes all of them.
issues.fix: Report the association; test whether irrigation explains the residuals (H3) and keep climate as a caveat.

issues.text: 'Buys less grain' can be the average (Y/N) or the marginal (dY/dN) return.
issues.fix: The marginal return is read from the fitted curve (mp); the average, grain_per_kg_fert, is tested directly.

issues.text: Fertiliser and yield years differ between countries, and fertiliser counts all three nutrients on arable land only.
issues.fix: Show the years on hover; drop countries where the arable-land denominator is meaningless.

alternatives.question: Within one country over 20 years, does yield still rise with fertiliser use (paths)?
alternatives.why: Drills into a country, removing the cross-country confounders.

alternatives.question: Do countries on the flat part (mp < 3) have larger nitrogen surpluses per hectare?
alternatives.why: Expands to the environmental cost: needs FAOSTAT's soil nutrient budget.

alternatives.question: Does the curve's ceiling rise with irrigated share?
alternatives.why: Drills into the main confounder already on the board.

hypotheses.statement: Cereal yield increases with fertiliser use per hectare.
hypotheses.null: Yield does not change with fertiliser use.

hypotheses.statement: The grain bought per kg of fertiliser falls as fertiliser use rises (diminishing returns).
hypotheses.null: Grain per kg of fertiliser is the same at every rate (yield proportional to fertiliser).

hypotheses.statement: Countries with more irrigated land yield more than the curve predicts.
hypotheses.null: The curve's residuals do not depend on the irrigated share.

concepts.label: Country's cropland
concepts.description: One country's arable land, latest year.

concepts.label: Fertiliser use
concepts.description: kg of N + P₂O₅ + K₂O per ha of arable land.

concepts.label: Cereal yield
concepts.description: kg of cereals harvested per ha.

concepts.label: Partial factor productivity
concepts.description: kg of grain per kg of fertiliser.

concepts.label: Yield residual
concepts.description: Observed against the fitted curve, in %.
concepts.why: What the curve leaves unexplained, H3's outcome.

strategy.detail: resid_pct = 100 · (yield_kg_ha / yield_pred − 1), yield_pred from the Mitscherlich fit

concepts.label: Nitrogen surplus
concepts.description: N input minus N removed in the harvest, kg/ha.

strategy.detail: FAOSTAT soil nutrient budget (domain ESB), matched on ISO3 country code and year

data.request: Cropland nitrogen surplus and nitrogen use efficiency per country, latest year
data.why: To test whether the flat part of the curve is where nitrogen is lost.

data.request: Mean growing-season temperature and precipitation over each country's cropland
data.source: Open-Meteo historical weather (ERA5) at cropland centroids, or the World Bank Climate Knowledge Portal
data.why: The ceiling of the curve depends on climate.

method.summary: A straight line of each outcome on its predictor with a weak prior (H1, H2: on fert_kg_ha; H3: resid_pct on irrigated_pct); the effect's 95% interval and P(direction). The saturating shape itself is fitted by the Mitscherlich grid search on the board, and compared with the straight line by R².

steps.title: Latest fertiliser use, cereal yield, arable land, irrigation
steps.detail: World Bank AG.CON.FERT.ZS, AG.YLD.CREL.KG, AG.LND.ARBL.HA, AG.LND.IRIG.AG.ZS, joined on iso3; aggregates dropped.

steps.title: Which countries the per-hectare figure fits
steps.detail: in_fit: arable_ha ≥ 200,000 and fert_kg_ha ≤ 800; why_out says why the rest are out.

steps.title: Fit the response curve
steps.detail: Grid search over c (150 values), closed-form A and Y0, profile interval of c; yield_pred, mp, resid_pct per country.

steps.title: Regressions
steps.detail: H1 yield_kg_ha on fert_kg_ha, H2 grain_per_kg_fert on fert_kg_ha, H3 resid_pct on irrigated_pct.

steps.title: Diminishing returns?
steps.detail: H1 and H2 supported and Mitscherlich R² > straight-line R²; H3 tells how much irrigation is in the curve.

caveats: Cross-country association, not a dose-response: richer countries irrigate more, use better seed and machinery and grow different cereals.
Fertiliser counts N + P₂O₅ + K₂O on arable land only; fertiliser on pasture or permanent crops inflates the rate (hence the exclusions).
Latest years differ between indicators and countries; a single year's yield carries its weather.
H2 is partly mechanical: Y/N falls with N unless yield is proportional to N; the null is that proportionality.
The ecological fallacy: a national average curve is not a farm's or a field's response.
